hook.en: On the night of 8 November 2016, most of the cash in people's wallets stopped being legal tender. Banks had long queues, and digital wallets suddenly became popular.
hook.kn: 8 ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2016ರ ರಾತ್ರಿ ಜನರ ಕೈಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದ ಬಹುಪಾಲು ನಗದು ಕಾನೂನುಬದ್ಧ ಹಣವಾಗಿ ಉಳಿಯಲಿಲ್ಲ. ಬ್ಯಾಂಕುಗಳ ಮುಂದೆ ಸಾಲು; ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್ ಪಾವತಿ ಜನಪ್ರಿಯವಾಯಿತು.

narration.en: On the night of 8 November 2016, most of the cash in people's wallets stopped being legal tender. Banks had long queues, and digital wallets suddenly became popular.
narration.kn: 8 ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2016ರ ರಾತ್ರಿ ಜನರ ಕೈಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದ ಬಹುಪಾಲು ನಗದು ಕಾನೂನುಬದ್ಧ ಹಣವಾಗಿ ಉಳಿಯಲಿಲ್ಲ. ಬ್ಯಾಂಕುಗಳ ಮುಂದೆ ಸಾಲು; ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್ ಪಾವತಿ ಜನಪ್ರಿಯವಾಯಿತು.

body.en: On 8 November 2016, the Government of India announced that ₹500 and ₹1000 notes would no longer be legal tender. People could deposit or exchange the old notes in banks within a time limit. New ₹500 and ₹2000 notes were issued.

points.en: Old ₹500 and ₹1000 notes ceased to be legal tender
Old notes could be deposited in bank accounts

narration.en: On 8 November 2016, the Government of India announced that ₹500 and ₹1000 notes would no longer be legal tender. People could deposit or exchange the old notes in banks within a time limit. New ₹500 and ₹2000 notes were issued.
narration.kn: 8 ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2016ರಂದು ₹500 ಮತ್ತು ₹1000 ನೋಟುಗಳು ಕಾನೂನುಬದ್ಧ ಹಣವಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಘೋಷಿಸಿತು. ಹಳೆಯ ನೋಟುಗಳನ್ನು ಬ್ಯಾಂಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಜಮಾ ಅಥವಾ ವಿನಿಮಯ ಮಾಡಬಹುದಿತ್ತು.

narration.en: Watch the board as we build this up step by step.

say.en: Cash flowed from homes into banks. Draw the flow.
Feature one: it is a tax administration measure; unaccounted cash comes into the open.
Feature two: it aims to curb corruption, black money and fake notes.
Feature three: it channelises savings into the formal financial system.
Feature four: it pushes India towards a less-cash, digital economy.

body.en: Demonetisation is seen as a tax administration measure that brings unaccounted cash into the open. It was also a measure to curb corruption, counterfeit currency and terror financing, to channelise savings into the formal financial system, and to create a less-cash economy.

points.en: Curbing corruption, fake currency and terror funding
Channelising savings into the formal system

narration.kn: ನೋಟು ಅಮಾನ್ಯೀಕರಣ ತೆರಿಗೆ ಆಡಳಿತ ಕ್ರಮ, ಭ್ರಷ್ಟಾಚಾರ ತಡೆ ಕ್ರಮ, ಉಳಿತಾಯವನ್ನು ಔಪಚಾರಿಕ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಗೆ ತರುವ ಮತ್ತು ಕಡಿಮೆ ನಗದು ಆರ್ಥಿಕತೆ ರೂಪಿಸುವ ಕ್ರಮ.

narration.en: The withdrawn notes made up a very large share of the cash in circulation, roughly 86 percent by value. Move the slider to see how big the share was.

label.en: Withdrawn notes, out of about ₹18 lakh crore

tryThis.en: At about 86%, how much cash had to be exchanged or deposited?
Why did this create long bank queues?
Why did digital payments grow so fast after this?

problem.en: After November 2016, a Davanagere cloth merchant who used to deal only in cash opened a current account, registered for UPI payments and began recording all his sales. Which features of demonetisation are seen?

steps.en: Moving from cash to UPI: towards a less-cash, digital economy.
Depositing cash and recording sales in a bank: channelising savings into the formal system.
Recorded sales can be assessed for tax: a tax administration measure.

answer.en: Less-cash economy, formal savings, and tax administration.

narration.en: Recap. On 8 November 2016, old ₹500 and ₹1000 notes ceased to be legal tender. It was a tax administration and anti-corruption measure. It pushed savings into banks and promoted digital payments.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. 8 ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2016ರಂದು ಹಳೆಯ ₹500, ₹1000 ನೋಟುಗಳು ರದ್ದಾದವು. ಇದು ತೆರಿಗೆ ಆಡಳಿತ ಮತ್ತು ಭ್ರಷ್ಟಾಚಾರ ವಿರೋಧಿ ಕ್ರಮ. ಇದು ಉಳಿತಾಯವನ್ನು ಬ್ಯಾಂಕಿಗೆ ತಂದು ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್ ಪಾವತಿ ಉತ್ತೇಜಿಸಿತು.
